title: Structural Dominance of Marginalized DAG Models under Edge Probing
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < field floor 7.4; restricted matched-menu scope and no causal-analysis consequence beyond the separator cap the sound result at subfield.

That restricted operational scope, and the absence of a consequence beyond the separator showing how the classification changes a causal analysis, constrain its score at a leading econometrics journal.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a finite three-part conditional normal form, fixed and universal-cardinality dominance, protected-cut port orbit/minimality results, and a same-mDAG XOR separator; the math referee passed these results. The field claim collapsed because the classification covers matched full-port menus and supplies no further causal-analysis consequence, while the promised partial-law diagonal bridge was left unstated. Restoring that bridge is established and non-material; a field-level continuation would require a new classification of genuinely restricted intervention menus.
tldr: For finite classical three-part DAGs with parentless inputs and childless visible outputs, the complete conditional model is exactly the independent-facet response family of the projected 3-mDAG. Its fixed-input dominance order is face inclusion together with input-to-output incidence inclusion; this also characterizes dominance across all nonempty finite visible alphabet choices. Cutting each original observed-source edge into a protected input root yields a port-specific footprint invariant, a whole-table orbit order, and a coarsest equivalence invariant for matched nontrivial typed menus.
gap: Node-probe mDAG equivalence does not classify graph-specific original-edge controls, and existing maximal interruption does not state a complete original-DAG port-law invariant.
fill: Establish or refute a finite face-and-footprint normal form, derive its fixed-matching and whole-table-orbit order, and expose the operational change caused by ordinary exogenization.
